formats.key: deposit(bytes pubkey, bytes withdrawal_credentials, bytes signature, bytes32 deposit_data_root)
effects: The signer sends msg.value in ETH (at least 1 ETH, a whole number of gwei) to the deposit contract, and the contract has no function that returns it.
The deposit is credited on the consensus layer to the validator named by pubkey.
The withdrawal_credentials decide who can withdraw the stake and rewards later; for a 0x01 or 0x02 credential, this is the address in bytes 12-32.
The signature and deposit_data_root only make the call valid: they are checked against the other inputs and move no assets.
formats.shown: "Stake ETH" with the validator public key and the withdrawal credentials as raw hex, and the ETH amount (e.g. "32 ETH"); the signature and the deposit data root are hidden.

findings.title: deposit shows withdrawal credentials as raw bytes32, so the withdrawal address is hard to see.
findings.evidence: descriptor.json, deposit format: {"label": "Withdraw credentials", "format": "raw", "path": "#.withdrawal_credentials"}; case 0 shows "0x0100000000000000000000007e2a2fa2a064f693f0a55c5639476d913ff12d05". The address that gets the stake is in bytes 12-32. DepositContract.deposit only checks withdrawal_credentials.length == 32. A 0x00 credential is a BLS key hash, so an address slice would be wrong for that type, and no single format fits every credential type.
findings.fix: Think about adding a second field "Withdrawal address" with path "#.withdrawal_credentials.[12:32]" and format addressName, and keep the raw field for the prefix. Label the raw field "Withdrawal credentials".

findings.title: deposit to an existing validator pubkey tops it up, and the withdrawal credentials shown are ignored.
findings.evidence: DepositContract.deposit (deposit_contract.sol) emits DepositEvent(pubkey, withdrawal_credentials, amount, ...) and does nothing else. The consensus layer decides the outcome: if the pubkey already exists, it keeps that validator's existing credentials. The descriptor shows "Withdraw credentials" as if they always apply.
findings.fix: No descriptor change can read consensus-layer state. A label such as "Withdrawal credentials (new validator only)" could help.

findings.title: deposit has one test only: a 32 ETH deposit with 0x01 credentials.
findings.evidence: cases/0.json: value 32000000000000000000, withdrawal_credentials prefix 0x01. No case has a 1 ETH top-up or 0x00/0x02 credentials, and the code accepts msg.value >= 1 ether.
findings.fix: Add a case with a smaller top-up amount and one with 0x02 compounding credentials.

cases.notes: The 32 ETH out matches "Amount to deposit: 32 ETH". The reader also read the withdrawal address correctly from the raw credentials.
